title: A diluted dye sample

answer:
Correct the measured absorbance for the blank:

\[
A_{\text{dye},1\,\text{cm}}=0.420-0.020=0.400
\]

Using Beer–Lambert law,

\[
A=\varepsilon c l
\]

For the diluted sample in the 1.00 cm cell:

\[
c_{\text{dil}}=\frac{0.400}{(8000)(1.00)}
=5.00\times10^{-5}\ \text{mol/L}
\]

Dilution factor:

\[
\frac{50.0\ \text{mL}}{10.0\ \text{mL}}=5.00
\]

Thus the original concentration is:

\[
c_{\text{orig}}=(5.00)(5.00\times10^{-5})
=2.50\times10^{-4}\ \text{mol/L}
\]

\[
\boxed{c_{\text{orig}}=2.50\times10^{-4}\ \text{M}
=0.000250\ \text{M}\approx0.250\ \text{mM}}
\]

For the diluted sample in a 2.00 cm cell, the dye absorbance doubles:

\[
A_{\text{dye},2\,\text{cm}}=2(0.400)=0.800
\]

If the blank is a fixed detector offset:

\[
A_{\text{obs}}=0.800+0.020=\boxed{0.820}
\]

If the blank scales with path length, then the blank absorbance at 2.00 cm is

\[
A_{\text{blank},2\,\text{cm}}=0.020(2.00)=0.040
\]

so

\[
A_{\text{obs}}=0.800+0.040=\boxed{0.840}
\]

Final answers:

\[
\boxed{c_{\text{original}}=2.50\times10^{-4}\ \text{mol/L}}
\]

For the diluted sample in a 2.00 cm cell:

\[
\boxed{A_{\text{fixed offset}}=0.820}
\]

\[
\boxed{A_{\text{blank scales with path length}}=0.840}
\]

All absorbances are in absorbance units.
